terms.definition: One of the numbers multiplied together in a multiplication problem.
terms.function: States the number of groups and the size of each group.
terms.whereItIs: The 3 (rows) and 4 (columns) labels on the array.
terms.whyItMatters: Factors are the inputs of multiplication and the building blocks of the product.

terms.definition: The result of multiplying factors together.
terms.function: Answers 'how many in all?' when groups are equal.
terms.whereItIs: The plate showing 12 beneath the array.
terms.whyItMatters: The product is what multiplication problems are solved to find.

terms.definition: An arrangement of objects in rows and columns that shows a multiplication.
terms.function: Turns factor × factor = product into a visual grid.
terms.whereItIs: The 3-by-4 grid of dots in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Arrays connect multiplication to area and make commutative properties easy to see.

terms.definition: Adding the same number many times, which multiplication summarizes.
terms.whereItIs: Shown by the group-lighting layer that adds a row at a time.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the bridge from addition to multiplication.

terms.definition: The property that changing the order of factors does not change the product.
terms.whereItIs: Demonstrated when the array rotates 90 degrees without changing the total.
terms.whyItMatters: It lets you choose the easier order when memorizing or solving multiplication.
